Ollama vs LM Studio: Same GGUF and Local API Checks

Both served the same local Qwen GGUF in our M3 Pro exercise, including ordinary and streaming requests after a network-restricted process restart. Keep the workflow you can manage, then verify model IDs and API behavior before migrating. The check below reuses one small Python client; it does not rank generation quality or speed.

One GGUF file, four completed API checks

On an Apple M3 Pro with 18 GiB of physical memory reported by macOS 27.2.1, we imported Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M into both systems. The source file, Ollama model layer and LM Studio imported path have the same SHA-256. The 491,400,032-byte model was downloaded once; LM Studio imported a symbolic link to it.

The common requests used temperature 0, at most 32 output tokens and the prompt Reply with exactly LOCAL_OK and nothing else. Both accepted the API alias ipunk-small; the shared request body stayed unchanged while the base URL changed. Chat templates, runtime builds and all internal defaults were not controlled uniformly. No throughput, answer-quality or memory-efficiency winner follows from this exercise.

Reuse a file, then confirm the model identifier

Keep the GGUF in a location you intend to retain. In Ollama, create a Modelfile pointing to it and create a test model:

FROM /path/to/qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf
PARAMETER num_ctx 4096
ollama create ipunk-small -f Modelfile
ollama list

For LM Studio, the tested CLI supports linking an existing file rather than downloading it again:

lms import --symbolic-link --user-repo Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-GGUF /path/to/qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf
lms ls
lms load qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct --context-length 4096 --gpu max --parallel 1 --identifier ipunk-small
lms server start --bind 127.0.0.1 --port 1235

Use the key returned by lms ls. Our first attempt to load a filename-derived key returned Model not found; loading the listed key worked. The assigned API identifier was ipunk-small. Ollama listed ipunk-small:latest and also accepted ipunk-small in our requests.

For our isolated Ollama test we used port 11435; the usual local examples use 11434. Confirm your actual port. A symbolic link depends on the source file staying available: moving or deleting the source can break a later load. An API model name by itself does not prove equivalent weights; keep the file digest separately.

Check your own local API

Download the Python script, run it on your computer, then open the resulting report here. It sends only the synthetic LOCAL_OK request to the loopback address you choose. It does not load a new model or expose a server to the network. Python 3 is required; there are no third-party Python packages to install.

Download probe-local-api.py

python3 probe-local-api.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:1235/v1 --model ipunk-small --label lmstudio --output lmstudio-report.json

If your server requires authentication, set LOCAL_LLM_API_KEY in your local environment. The script does not put the key in its JSON report, follows no redirects and ignores proxy settings for these local requests. You do not need to enable broad browser CORS access. Imported reports stay in this tab; a downloaded record remains on your device.

A completed report means the client received a model list, a normal response and a finished stream. Exact text matching is a separate field. The worksheet cannot verify model-file hashes, who actually ran the server, or whether external networking was blocked.

What our restricted restart proves

After an ordinary successful run, we stopped each test service and launched its process through a macOS sandbox policy that denies outbound networking except loopback. The model and inference runtime were already cached. Both returned LOCAL_OK through the same ordinary and streaming requests after restart.

A control HTTP server on loopback remained reachable; an explicit external-IP connection in a process using the same policy failed with PermissionError, errno 1. The computer itself stayed online. This is a process-level restart check with a warm filesystem cache, not a machine reboot, an empty-cache installation, a packet audit or a general privacy guarantee.

Ollama restricted-run report · LM Studio restricted-run report · Control checks and method · Process policy

If a restart fails, distinguish a missing model or runtime download from an incorrect model ID, blocked authentication or a failed inference request. A working local service with cached files does not establish every feature’s behavior without internet access.
